4 ارتب الكَعْبَ , (T, M, A,) inf. n. إِرْتَابٌ, (T,) said of a boy, (T, M, A,) He made the كعب [i. e. cockal-bone, or die,] to stand erect, or upright: (T, * A:) or he made the كعب firm, or steady. (M.) ＝
-A2- ارتب as an intrans. v.: see 1. ＝
-A3- Also, inf. n. as above, He became a beggar, after having been rich, or in a state of competence. (IAar, T, K. [Perhaps formed by transposition from أَتْرَبَ.]) ＝
-A4- And He invited distinguished persons to his food, or banquet. (T.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
